summit.title: Terraces, a counter and the open sea
summit.story: Split's grand tables split between the palace, the harbour and the sea. ZOI is built into the palace's south façade with a top-floor terrace over the Riva; Gault&Millau scores it 17/20 in 2026 and MICHELIN has recommended it since it opened in 2017. Krug, on the harbour front, is a counter of about twelve seats round an open kitchen, and in the 2025 guide it became the first table in the city to hold a MICHELIN star. Dvor, at Firule, a short walk east, faces the open channel from a garden terrace and scores 16/20. None publishes a winter schedule, and Dvor has historically closed for one: call before you promise any of them after October.
summit.where: ZOI, Riva; Krug, Obala Ante Trumbića; Dvor, Firule

varos.title: Grills of the fishermen's quarter
varos.story: Veli Varoš, the old quarter of fishermen and farmers below Marjan, cooks the catch with little fuss: fish is shown raw, priced by weight and grilled. Konoba Fetivi on Tomića stine is the one with a 2026 MICHELIN listing, and Gault&Millau praises its black cuttlefish risotto. Its neighbour, Konoba Matejuška, is a small family grill named for the fishermen's harbour below, known for tuna marinated in red wine and herbs. Šperun, on the short street of the same name at the quarter's edge, grills sardines and sea bass until late. Only Fetivi has a guide rating; the other two are neighbourhood tables, so call ahead.
varos.where: Konoba Fetivi, Veli Varoš; Konoba Matejuška, Matejuška; Šperun Eat and Drink, Veli Varoš

palace.title: Kitchens in and around the walls
palace.story: People still live inside Diocletian's walls, and the kitchens in and around them range from a market counter to a Gothic townhouse. Villa Spiza, on Kružićeva, is a box of a room where Ivana Gamulin cooks what she bought that morning, takes cash only and no bookings. Apetit occupies an upper floor of the 15th-century Papalić Palace and keeps the old dishes, pašticada and even tripe. Bokeria, just outside the west wall beside the fish market, is the modern wine bistro of the three, glass-fronted and lined with bottles, at 13.5/20 with Gault&Millau. Villa Spiza works winter hours; the others publish none.
palace.where: Villa Spiza, Palace; Apetit, Papalić Palace; Bokeria Kitchen & Wine, fish market

canteen.title: Lunch where Split eats
canteen.story: Split's everyday tables cook from the morning fish market and the family stove, not from a tasting menu. Buffet Fife has fed the Matejuška waterfront for decades from two buildings and a terrace, with pašticada and gnocchi, fish soup and fried squid at prices the locals still pay; Tripadvisor reviews show it trading through the 2026 summer and it reportedly works all year. Konoba Marjan, a few tables on Senjska in Veli Varoš, is run by a father, mother and son who change the menu daily with the fish market, so the cuttlefish brujet or black risotto can be gone by half past seven. Neither publishes a winter schedule, so call before you go.
canteen.where: Buffet Fife, Matejuška; Konoba Marjan, Veli Varoš

glass.title: Croatian wine by the glass
glass.story: Zinfandel is a Dalmatian grape under another name: DNA work at UC Davis in 2001 traced it to Tribidrag, also called Crljenak Kaštelanski, found in the Kaštela vineyards outside Split. Zinfandel Food & Wine Bistro on Marulićeva takes its name from that story, pours about fifteen Croatian wines by the glass, and is in the MICHELIN Guide Croatia 2026. Paradox, which opened in 2012 and from 2017 poured only Croatian wine in a Secession-era room behind the Riva, is now reported permanently closed by several listings, so for now the old town's serious wine glass is at Zinfandel.
glass.where: Zinfandel Food & Wine Bistro, Centre; PARADOX Wine & Cheese Bar, Riva (reported closed)

street.title: Markets and the fishermen's buffet
street.story: Split eats on its feet in the morning. The Pazar green market trades daily against the east wall of Diocletian's Palace by the Silver Gate, where family farms sell figs, greens, olive oil and Pag cheese from about six until early afternoon. A few minutes west, the Ribarnica off Marmontova sells the night's catch by weight, in cash, until about one. And at Matejuška, Buffet Fife has fed the waterfront for decades with pašticada and gnocchi, fish soup and fried squid at prices the locals still pay; it reportedly works all year. None of the three takes a booking.
street.where: Pazar, Silver Gate; Ribarnica, Marmontova; Buffet Fife, Matejuška

bistro.title: The wine list first
bistro.where: Zinfandel Food & Wine Bistro, Centre; Šug, Tolstojeva
bistro.story: Split's newer tables start from the glass. Zinfandel, on Marulićeva, takes its name from the Kaštela vines whose story is told above, pours about fifteen Croatian wines by the glass and is in the MICHELIN Guide Croatia 2026. Šug, a small stone room on Tolstojeva by the palace's north-east corner, cooks braised pot dishes and held a MICHELIN Bib Gourmand from 2022; Gault&Millau scores it 13.5/20 in 2026. Both are small and both publish hours that disagree with one another's listings, so book at night and call in winter.

locals.title: Where the city eats
locals.where: Konoba Marjan, Veli Varoš; Kantun Paulina, Matošića
locals.story: Split's everyday tables cook from the morning fish market and the charcoal, not from a tasting menu. Konoba Marjan, a few tables on Senjska at the foot of the hill, is run by a father, mother and son who change the menu daily with the market, so the cuttlefish brujet or black risotto can be gone by half past seven. Kantun Paulina, on Matošića near Marmontova, has grilled ćevapi for decades and serves them the Split way, in a soft lepinja with ajvar and raw onion, by small, medium or large, cash only. Neither publishes a winter schedule: call or look in.
